sources_read: .qc-cache/coldwater-editor-2026-10-02-r1/rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx:Quality Checks!A30:D30 and Internal Quality Checks!A30:D30; both rubric sheets enumerated
evidence: The actual workbook Quality Checks row 29 requires the real render/constraints gate and an in-dimension hard zero for blank/static-shell apps in every scored prompt; its public-network wording supersedes the obsolete cross-origin phrase in Internal Quality Checks row 29. Positive: tests/gates/render/judge.toml:23 requires a keyboard-authored JS Run with two increasing preview and console totals; tests/gates/constraints/judge.toml:23 requires a custom editing surface, and :32 requires a new saved snippet read in an independent clean browser context. tests/scoring.toml:1-11 gives both gates zero reward mass; tests/test.sh:212-227 runs gates before scored, and tests/tools/score.py:40-48 zeroes reward on gate failure. The prompts at tests/scored/{functional,polish,visual}/prompt.md:1 are identical common instructions and contain no pre-scoring check or instruction to assign zero to all dimension criteria when the app is blank, broken, or a static shell; each says a missing feature fails only its owner and a prior failure must not erase independent evidence. Visual prompt.md:5 further limits judgment to screenshots, while visual/judge.toml:24,34,44 offer a 1-point anchor even for missing or unusable presentation. The frozen template's scored prompts explicitly say 'If the gate fails, assign 0 to every criterion in this dimension' (each scored prompt's Global browser gate section), showing the omitted contract. A second hard-gate defect is constraints/judge.toml:32: it demands 'a successful application write response containing its exact title, filename and source.' The public requirement in environment/instructions/behaviour.md:9 is to save those fields and read the record fresh; integration.md:5 lets authors choose routes and frontend tools. It does not require the write response to echo fields. A 204 or ID-only successful Save followed by exact fresh server readback would therefore fail this all_pass gate. No sign-in is required (instruction.md:5; tests/app_context.md:3). All actual prompts allow public assets at :1 and impose no same-origin test. The raw-evidence-index.json named by the assignment was absent when checked; no full judge or mutant-app result is claimed. SHA256 was computed for the inspected frozen gate and scored prompts and gate judge files; the assigned input_sha256 was preserved, not independently reconstructed.
counterexample: Conforming alternative that fails: an app saves exact title, filename and source on its server, returns HTTP 204 from Save, then supplies the exact record to a new clean browser context through its normal library and again after reload. It meets behaviour.md:9 and integration.md:7 but fails constraints/judge.toml:32 solely because the write response has no echoed fields. Plausible broken app that could receive scored-dimension credit if the scored suite is invoked independently or the earlier gate observation becomes stale: a styled static playground shell with focusable controls and editor-looking text, but no working editing, execution or server-backed Save. The visual criteria's 1-point missing/unusable anchors and absence of an in-dimension hard-zero instruction leave room for nonzero scores despite the shell. The normal gate-first score.py path would correctly zero this shell if the gates themselves are judged accurately; this latter risk is prompt-level and unmeasured.
suggested_fix: Keep the real gates, but change the saved-record gate to require an observed successful Save plus exact independent-context server readback, without prescribing echoed write-response fields. Add an explicit pre-scoring browser gate to each of the functional, polish and visual prompts that assigns zero to every criterion if the app is blank, broken, or a static shell, including the applicable server-backed check; allow public off-origin assets and data transport, and retain the no-sign-in contract.
